deviations.what: per-record writer segments (a clone only on a change of writer) diffed at commit, instead of cursor ranges per system call plus one step-end diff per entity
deviations.why: every field gets its own writer even when two writers touch one record in one substep; cost stays proportional to the records written

deviations.what: set_quiet writes logged at the write as physical and left out of that frame's record diffs
deviations.why: 6.2 makes quiet writes physical; the kernel thermal model writes hundreds per frame (kept in a lazily merged tail for the 15 % budget)

deviations.what: substep settle robot attribution from the kernel physics' consequence records (by robot)
deviations.why: the same rule impact.robot_caused already applies (the robot arranged the item or its support)

deviations.what: finish keeps the failures at D and drops F's clock-only labels (budget, deadline:*)
deviations.why: the budget is judged at D (8.1); a failure holding when the robot declared done stays a failure

deviations.what: fast_forward is a step; 'activity in the robot's room' = an agent's position, posture, activity, awake or state changing there; no watched zone
deviations.why: it replaces a WAIT plan step; mere presence of a sleeping resident forced fine ticks in most houses; the per-spec equivalence check decides

deviations.what: extra keys: logs.gone 'name'; mess flows 'op', 't0', 'n', 'name', 'cause', src class created:, dst class loss:
deviations.why: 6.5's created:<step> origins and loss:<cause> sinks need classes; names help review
